snippet.textDisplay: You can never save enough money for care in your later years. I say this because I have seen it in my own family where my parents and grandparents were needing care beyond what they could do themselves for years. My grandma needing more and more care for 14 years before she passed away from Alzheimers. My dad needed 5 years of increasingly more care. My grandmother used up the money she and my grandpa saved, money saved that they hoped to use after retirement to travel. She then had to go on Medicaid. She was in memory care facilities for her entire illness, aside from being in her home for 5 years, before her illness made it too dangerous for her to be home alone. My dad is home with us, our lives have been on hold caregiving for my dad as his care increased. What we have learned is that we as Americans are living longer, but not necessarily healthier. Money goes so quick when you have so many medical expenses, surgeries, doctors visits, medication, care at home, care in a facility, personal care items, etc. Speak with a financial planner for you or your family members expected needs before retirement, while you or your parents are in relatively good health.

snippet.textDisplay: Very touchy subject for our family right now. My husband and I are in our late thirties, we have two daughters, one in primary school and one in kindergarten. His mom just turned 70yo and now insists we have to live together, she is great health wise, and from past experiences with her, when she spends some months with us, she does nothing, she just sits on the couch and does nothing at all, doesn't cook a meal, doesn't make her bed, doesn't go grocery shopping...and being an active person is what keeps you alive and awake, is what keeps you from suddenly becoming an elderly person who needs care....she wants we move with her which means us leaving our jobs, our home and school to move to a place where there would be no job opportunities for me specially as a foreigner and where our daughters would have to go to a, quite honestly, far away and bad school. And if she moves in with us...we have three bedrooms which is the largest you usually find for apartments, and we live in a city, so she doesn't like it...but also we think...are we really gonna get into this situation now in our late thirties? can this not wait another 8-10 years or so?my grandma is 89, my mom lives with her and in my grandma's words..."you do that now that is medically not necessary and you may be sharing your home with her for +20 years"...and it scares us because our marriage would also be affected by it, is not only our personal space, our finances, and our free time..is also our relationship with our daughters and our own marriage....my husband was raised by his grandparents and only saw his mom once a year, she actually only visited us once since we became parents in 2018, and 3 times in 14 years, where we live is common for grandparents to be very supportive and she wasn't involved at all...but now she comes with this demand..so here we are ..

snippet.textDisplay:
As far as other cultures go… Indian family lives next door to me. 6 people in the home. 2 parents, 2 young children, 2 grandparents. The grandparents are active. They cook, clean, help with the children, garden and yard work. If and when they become debilitated, I’m sure they will be taken cared for, but they also put in years of work for their son’s family.
Independence is valued more in the U.S. The people currently in their 80s and 90s retired in their early 60s. then they spent the next decades, relaxing and enjoying themselves. Why, then, should people in their 50s and 60s be expected to give up their lives to care for them? You don’t OWE your parents the last healthy decades of YOUR life. Many people don’t take care of their health or their finances and end up in bad situations later in life.

snippet.textDisplay: Having a Living Will and Trust is vital. It is MORE DETAILED than a "Will." A "Will" does NOT PREVENT property owned by a parent to go through Probate Court. A "Will" means property GOES through PROBATE COURT and it is very expensive. Probate Court will tie up property as well as your inheritance for up to 1 year (maybe more) depending on what State you live in, so make sure YOU GET ALL YOUR Legal documents in order for your elderly parent. Don't put it off.

My plan is to work as long as I can, then make myself comfortable and let nature take its course.

snippet.textDisplay: This is never easy, from the rich to the person living on SSI. I don’t want my kids to worry about caring for me, but this is such a stark reality for me and my husband (I’m 43, work for Aging and People with Disabilities). Don’t focus so much on yourself and your career, but love everyone around you. We have saved and invested, but if you sell your property for $1 million… split that between 2 people… that’s $500k per person, divide by conservatively about $7500 a month for assisted living (not nursing facility level of care), that is about 66 months of payment, which means (without inflation each month) 5 1/2 years of living in ALF… is that enough? I do not want my children to halt their lives, dreams, hopes, destiny to try to support the ongoing demise of me. So people… as a person who has worked in this industry for years… love the people around you (kids, family, neighbors, friends, colleagues, etc.), every little bit helps. Towards the end of the trajectory of our lives, what did we leave in this world? A burden? Or love, laughter, beauty, and joy? ❤
